claims.claim: Hebrew is a caseless (unicameral) script: the widely used modern scripts with case are Latin, Greek, Armenian and Cyrillic, so text-transform: uppercase/capitalize and small-caps are no-ops on Hebrew letters while still transforming embedded Latin.
claims.raw_snippet: The most widely used modern scripts with case are Latin, Greek, Armenian and Cyrillic.
claims.verified_via: Unicode case-mapping FAQ fetched; page also states "The vast majority of scripts, modern or archaic, do not have case distinctions."

claims.claim: Intl.DateTimeFormat('he-IL') resolves to the Gregorian calendar; the Hebrew calendar is requested via the `ca` Unicode extension key, e.g. Intl.DateTimeFormat('he-IL-u-ca-hebrew'), which formats 2026-09-20 as '9 בתשרי 5787'.
claims.raw_snippet: The calendar to use, such as "chinese", "gregory", "persian", and so on. For a list of supported calendar types, see Intl.supportedValuesOf(); the default is locale dependent. This option can also be set through the ca Unicode extension key; if both are provided, this options property takes precedence.
claims.verified_via: MDN DateTimeFormat options fetched; behaviour confirmed locally: new Intl.DateTimeFormat('he-IL').resolvedOptions().calendar === 'gregory' and 'he-IL-u-ca-hebrew' formats 2026-09-20 as '9 בתשרי 5787'
